title: About a tenth of a flora's seeds could survive sea-drift across 900 miles

fields.label: Label
fields.value: About a tenth of a flora's seeds could survive sea-drift across 900 miles

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Based on flotation and germination experiments, the seeds of roughly 10 per cent of the plants of a flora, after drying, could be floated by sea currents across about 900 miles of sea and still germinate.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Therefore it would perhaps be safer to assume that the seeds of about 10/100 plants of a flora, after having been dried, could be floated across a space of sea 900 miles in width, and would then germinate.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XI, “Geographical Distribution”; section “Means of dispersal, by changes of climate and of the level of the land, and by occasional means”. Scope: seeds and fruits of flowering plants exposed to sea-water

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch11-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The numerical claim is highly operational and discriminating, but needed species-level experimental data are fragmented. Existing studies can estimate the proportion for selected floras, not robustly for a generic flora.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compile published seawater flotation-duration and post-immersion germination experiments for a representative flora, combine survival time with current velocities, and estimate the fraction capable of 900-mile dispersal. Confidence intervals excluding 10 percent would refute Darwin's numerical estimate.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ocean travel time depends strongly on route and seed state.

No known unified dataset samples a representative whole flora.

Published experiments may overrepresent dispersal-prone taxa.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.56
operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.39
discriminating power: 0.82
analysis feasibility: 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The fraction that survives a stated ocean crossing is a sharp numerical target. Existing trait databases cover buoyancy or seed morphology for some floras and do not contain the seawater-plus-germination trial at flora scale. A compiled subset of published experiments can bound the fraction for particular coasts and cannot confirm the one-tenth figure for a flora in general.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate the fraction of species in a regional flora whose dried seeds stay buoyant and then germinate after a seawater exposure long enough to cross about 900 miles. A flora-scale fraction far from one tenth, under that protocol, would refute the numerical claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Available buoyancy trials often use fresh water and omit germination after drying.

Transit time for 900 miles depends on a current speed the claim leaves implicit.

No public dataset applies one seawater flotation and germination protocol to a whole flora.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.4
data existence: 0.45
